title: Sort Colors
description:
Given an array `nums` with `n` objects colored red, white, or blue, sort them **in-place** so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red, white, and blue.

We use the integers `0`, `1`, and `2` to represent the color red, white, and blue, respectively.

You must solve this problem without using the library's sort function. Can you come up with a one-pass algorithm using only `O(1)` extra space?
hints: A two-pass counting sort works easily: count how many 0s, 1s, and 2s appear, then overwrite the array.
For a single-pass O(1)-space solution, apply Dijkstra's Dutch National Flag 3-way partitioning with three pointers: low, mid, and high.
Maintain the invariant: nums[0..low-1] are all 0s, nums[low..mid-1] are all 1s, nums[mid..high] are unexamined, and nums[high+1..n-1] are all 2s.

examples.explanation: All 0s are moved to the front, 1s to the middle, and 2s to the end: [0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2].
A single-element array is already sorted.
